description: The plot illustrates how accuracy (ACC) changes as a function of co-occurrence number for six methods (Base, FT, IKE, MEND, MEMIT, and ROME). The x-axis is labeled “Co-occurrence Number” and uses a logarithmic scale, spanning from 0 to about 10^3 (with major tick labels at 0, 10^1, 10^2, and 10^3); the plotted points appear at four increasing co-occurrence values (approximately around 5, 30, 300, and 3000). The y-axis is labeled “ACC (%)” on a linear scale from 60 to 85, with tick marks every 5 percentage points (60, 65, 70, 75, 80, 85). The Base line is black with circular markers and a solid line, increasing from about 64% at the smallest co-occurrence value to about 71% at the largest, with intermediate points near 66.5% and 69%. The FT line is blue with downward-triangle markers and a solid line, rising from about 65.5% to about 73%, passing through roughly 69% and 71.5%. The IKE line is red with upward-triangle markers and a solid line, increasing from about 67.5% to about 75%, with midpoints near 72% and 74.5%. The MEND line is brown with diamond markers and a solid line, rising from about 70.5% to about 80%, with intermediate values around 75.5% and 78.5%. The MEMIT line is purple with pentagon markers and a solid line, increasing from about 69.5% to about 77.5%, with midpoints near 74% and 77%. The ROME line is green with square markers and a solid line, increasing from about 74.5% to about 84%, with intermediate points around 79.5% and 82.5%.
